newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: W.African central bank sells bills at fixed 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: W.African central bank sells bills at fixed 4 pct.

text.p: The Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO) said on Tuesday that it sold 20.9 billion CFA francs ($33 million) of 28-day bills at its August 4 tender at a fixed rate of 4.0 percent.
Bank officials said that compared with the marginal rate of 4.70 percent at the previous tender on July 28. The average rate at that tender was 4.6410 percent.

Officials said the central bank has the possibility of offering a fixed rate tender whenever it chooses. They declined to say whether the lower rate had been intended as a signal to commercial banks to lower their lending rates.

This is the eighth tender the central bank has held this year, at weekly intervals beginning June 16, as part of its money market liquidity operations. During previous months it had been injecting liquidity.
The bank received offers for 20.9 billion CFA francs of bills from 11 operators and accepted them all.
It said its discount rate was unchanged at 6.25 percent.

The BCEAO is the central bank of the eight states that make up the West African part of the Franc Zone -- Benin, Burkina Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Ivory Coast, Mali, Niger, Senegal and Togo. ($ = 630 CFA francs)
